Driver.title: Driver
Driver.description: Represents a driver employed by Transportes Especiales J&J.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Driver entity.

licenseExpiryDate.description: The expiration date of the driver's license.

isActive.description: Indicates if the driver is currently active.

dateHired.description: The date when the driver was hired.

Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Represents a vehicle in the company's fleet.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vehicle entity.

year.description: The manufacturing year of the vehicle.

capacity.description: The passenger capacity of the vehicle.

lastMaintenanceDate.description: The date of the last scheduled maintenance.

status.description: The current operational status of the vehicle (e.g., 'Active', 'In Maintenance', 'Inactive').

currentDriverId.description: Reference to the currently assigned Driver. (Relationship: Driver 1:N Vehicle)

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer who uses transportation services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

name.description: The name of the customer (company or individual).

contactPerson.description: The primary contact person for the customer.

address.description: The primary billing or contact address of the customer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

description.description: A brief description of the service provided.

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer for whom the service is provided. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Service)

driverId.description: Reference to the Driver assigned to this service. (Relationship: Driver 1:N Service)

vehicleId.description: Reference to the Vehicle assigned to this service. (Relationship: Vehicle 1:N Service)

scheduledStartTime.description: The planned start time of the service.

scheduledEndTime.description: The planned end time of the service.

actualStartTime.description: The actual start time of the service (null if not started).

actualEndTime.description: The actual end time of the service (null if not completed).

originAddress.description: The starting address for the service route.

destinationAddress.description: The final destination address for the service route.

passengerCount.description: The number of passengers for this service.

status.description: The current status of the service (e.g., 'Scheduled', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled').

estimatedCost.description: The estimated cost of the service.

actualCost.description: The actual cost incurred for the service (null if not finalized).

VehicleLocation.title: VehicleLocation
VehicleLocation.description: Records real-time or historical location data for a vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VehicleLocation record.

vehicleId.description: Reference to the Vehicle whose location is being recorded. (Relationship: Vehicle 1:N VehicleLocation)

latitude.description: The latitude coordinate of the vehicle's location.

longitude.description: The longitude coordinate of the vehicle's location.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the location was recorded.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: Represents an invoice issued for completed services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Invoice entity.

serviceId.description: Reference to the Service for which this invoice is generated. (Relationship: Service 1:N Invoice)

customerId.description: Reference to the Customer associated with this invoice. (Relationship: Customer 1:N Invoice)

issueDate.description: The date when the invoice was issued.

dueDate.description: The date by which the invoice payment is due.

amount.description: The total amount of the invoice.

status.description: The current payment status of the invoice (e.g., 'Pending', 'Paid', 'Overdue', 'Cancelled').

paymentDate.description: The date when the invoice was paid (null if not paid).

paymentMethod.description: The method used for payment (null if not paid).

Expense.title: Expense
Expense.description: Tracks various operational expenses not directly tied to a specific service.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Expense entity.

amount.description: The monetary amount of the expense.

expenseDate.description: The date when the expense was incurred.

category.description: The category of the expense (e.g., 'Fuel', 'Maintenance', 'Driver Salary').

vehicleId.description: Optional reference to a Vehicle if the expense is directly related to it. (Relationship: Vehicle 0:N Expense)

driverId.description: Optional reference to a Driver if the expense is directly related to them. (Relationship: Driver 0:N Expense)

definition.description: This collection identifies users with administrative privileges. The mere existence of a document for a `userId` in this collection grants administrative access to internal application data. This enables Database Access Control (DBAC) without custom claims and supports authorization independence for all admin-restricted collections.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique ID of the user who possesses administrative privileges.

Each document's ID corresponds to the `vehicleId`, and it represents the most recent `VehicleLocation` update. Access restricted to authenticated administrators.

params.name: vehicleId
params.description: The unique identifier for the vehicle whose current location is stored.

definition.description: A dedicated, top-level collection for storing publicly viewable real-time tracking information for *active* services. Each document's ID is the `serviceId`. This collection ensures Authorization Independence by including denormalized fields such as `currentLatitude`, `currentLongitude`, `lastUpdatedTimestamp` (from `VehicleLocation` data), `serviceStatus`, and a critical `isPubliclyTrackable` boolean flag within the document itself. This design directly supports the `/gps/[id]` public route with simple, atomic security rules, as all required authorization context is self-contained.

params.name: serviceId
params.description: The unique identifier for the service being publicly tracked.

params.description: The unique identifier for an expense.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
This design primarily achieves authorization independence for publicly accessible data through explicit denormalization. For instance, the `/publicServiceTracking/{serviceId}` collection is critical for the `/gps/[id]` public route. Each document in this collection directly contains all necessary public authorization context, such as the `isPubliclyTrackable` boolean flag, along with denormalized location and service status data. This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in Firestore Security Rules to check parent `Service` documents for permissions, allowing for atomic and highly performant reads for public users. Internal data (e.g., Drivers, Vehicles, Services) relies on the existence of a user's UID in the `/adminUsers/{userId}` collection, which is also an independent, atomic check.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters) and Structural Segregation:**
Structural segregation is applied to ensure a homogeneous security posture within collections. For example, internal `VehicleLocation` history is kept in `/vehicles/{vehicleId}/locationHistory/{locationRecordId}` or real-time internal status in `/currentVehicleLocations/{vehicleId}` – both are restricted to authenticated administrators. In contrast, publicly trackable service data resides in the dedicated `/publicServiceTracking/{serviceId}` collection. This segregation ensures that public data does not share collections with sensitive internal data, simplifying security rules significantly. QAPs are supported as rules can directly assert permissions based on document IDs (e.g., `request.auth.uid == userId` for private user data) or specific document fields (e.g., `resource.data.isPubliclyTrackable == true` for public data), enabling efficient and secure `get()` and `list()` operations without acting as filters. For admin-facing collections, a simple `allow list: if exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/adminUsers/$(request.auth.uid));` rule ensures that listing all documents is secure and efficient for authorized users.
